global: Let the chroniclers record it: {player} fled the field with a broken standard and a lighter purse. A fitting end for a bold tongue.
The banners of {player} were trampled today. Let no minstrel sing of that rout in our halls.
{player} charged like a prophet and fell like a lamb. Honour is a heavy coin, ser, and you could not pay it.
Another hero of the roads has gone home to nurse his pride. The mud of this field suits him well.
I bled {troop_count} men to take this hill and paid no more than a scratch. Let the lesser lords learn from it.
Say what you like of {player}, but the field remembers only who stood at the end. That was not you.
A sour morning for {player}. The dice of war rolled against them, and I gave them no mercy to hope for.
Let it be sung in every hall: {player} came with {troop_count} blades and left with none. Praise the ancestors for patience.
Pride goeth before a fall, and {player} tumbled from a great height today. I pity the horse who carried them.
Mark this day, friends. The ground drank the blood of {player} and found it thin and watery. Ser, you disappoint.
whisper: You fought well enough for one who sings his own praises, ser {player}. Ride home and tell your bards to lie better.
I will not pretend the field was kind to you, {player}. It was not. Keep your distance from my roads until you learn manners.
Your oath means little if your sword cannot keep it. Mine has kept every vow I made this week.
Think on this, {player}: the next time we meet, I will not spare you the indignity of a slow defeat.
A sorry business. {player} threw away a fine company of {troop_count} for a hill no one will remember.
Hear me, {player}. Your name is spoken with a smirk in my hall tonight, and I intend to keep it there.
The gold of {gold} you lost today will feed my men through the winter. Wear the loss as well as you can.
I bore no grudge when we began, ser {player}. I bear one now, and I shall carry it like a stone in my boot.
Do not mistake a single victory for a lasting peace. Your banners fell today and mine still fly.
Ser {player}, your retreat was so elegant I half suspected you had rehearsed it. Practice more before the next muster.
face: Stand where you are, {player}. You have tasted the dust of this field and found it bitter. Step aside, or taste more of it.
So the proud standard of {player} lies in the mud. Pick it up and carry it home, and remember the face of the one who knocked it down.
Ser {player}, I have no wish to spill more blood on a morning already soaked. Yield your road and be gone, before I forget my mercy.
You came at me with {troop_count} riders and a hundred boasts. Count the boasts again, friend. Only the riders remain on the field, and they are not yours.
Your sword is quick, ser {player}, but your judgement is slower. Learn that before you next lift a blade against me.
Bold words for a beaten knight. I would laugh if I did not still hear the cries of your wounded across the field.
The hill is mine and the day is mine. Ride back to your liege with my compliments and a warning that I am not forgiving.
I do not hate you, {player}. I hate the way you smile after losing, as if the loss were a jest between old friends.
A poor showing, ser. Your men stood like sheep before a wolf, and the wolf was not even hungry.
Turn your horse, {player}. Every step away from me is a step toward a better fight, and I will be waiting when you return.

global: The field is cleared and the day is done. {player} lost this round, and the roads will be quieter for it.
Hard fortune for {player} this morning. The wheel turns, and today it turned under their horse.
Honest battle today. {player} gave a fair account of themselves, though the day belonged to us.
Let the record show a victory for my banner over {player}, fought on open ground and settled before supper.
I took {troop_count} men into that valley and brought most of them back. Such is the arithmetic of the field.
Wars are won by the patient and lost by the proud. {player} was neither patient nor fortunate today.
A skirmish at the ford ends in our favour. The road to the eastern market is open again, for whatever that is worth.
Plenty of coin changed hands on that hill, {gold} at the least by my reckoning. The chroniclers may count it themselves.
No grudge is owed by either side after a clean fight. Ser {player} may take the road home with their dignity intact.
The rain began just as the last horn sounded. Some days the sky chooses a winner, and today it was not {player}.
whisper: Our meeting at the ridge was settled in my favour, ser {player}. I trust you will take it in good grace.
You fought with more discipline than I expected. I may choose to remember that when our paths cross next.
A word of plain advice: keep your flanks covered. The ground beyond the hill is not as friendly as it looks.
I have no quarrel with you, {player}, only with the outcome. The outcome is mine, and I am content with it.
The day went badly for you. Rest your horse before you ride on, and do not push him through the marsh.
There were {troop_count} of your banners on that ridge. I counted them twice, and I admire the stubbornness.
If you wish to discuss the terms of your surrender, ser {player}, I am open to hearing them over wine.
We fought, we won, and no oath was broken. I consider that an acceptable morning's work.
Pass my compliments to your captains. Their formation held longer than I thought it would.
{gold} was staked on this skirmish by people who never saw it. I wonder how they feel about the result.
face: Ser {player}, the field is ours and the road ahead is open. You may pass, provided you keep your swords sheathed.
Good day to you. I would have preferred a cleaner fight, but the sun is up and the dead do not complain.
You have lost this skirmish, traveller. Take the lesson and go. There is no shame in a fair defeat.
Hail, {player}. We met over this hill and one of us walked away. I am glad it was not a longer afternoon.
I hold this ridge now and I mean to keep it. Speak your business quickly, for my men are weary and so am I.
Our quarrel ended here, though I doubt it will stay ended. Men of your standing rarely accept a single defeat.
A plain question, ser {player}: will you bring your banners back to this road, or shall we leave them in the grass?
I have seen enough blood for one morning. Pass on, and do not give me cause to draw again.
The victory is mine, but it does not feel like much. Go home, friend, and tell your liege the field was cold.
No trick today, no ambush. Just a fair defeat and an honest road. Mind the stream when you cross it.

global: Ser {player} fought like a lion on this ridge, and I am proud to have shared the field with them, even in defeat.
A glorious contest, and a glorious loss. {player} wore their colours with honour to the last, and the ancestors will remember.
Let the bards sing of {player} tonight, for they went down swinging with {troop_count} stalwart men beside them.
The ridge belongs to us today, but the honour belongs to {player}. I name them worthy of a fairer day.
Hear, hear! {player} was a worthy opponent and a finer companion over the campfire. Long may their banners wave.
A hard fall for {player}, and a hard-won victory for us. Both sides earned their stories this morning.
Honour to ser {player}, who taught this field a lesson in stubbornness. We shall meet again over better wine.
I take no joy in this win, for {player} is a friend to the cause. The next muster is ours to share.
The ancestors watched closely today, and they saw {player} hold their ground longer than any could expect.
May the roads be kind to {player}. Such a valiant defeat should be followed by a long and peaceful rest.
whisper: My friend, that was a glorious clash. Take your rest and send word when you are ready for the next.
You fought me as an equal, ser {player}, and I think the better for it. My sword remains at your disposal.
Do not grieve too deeply for the hill, {player}. We shall have better fields, and I would have you beside me on them.
Your charge was the bravest sight I have seen this year. I will tell my sons of it when they are older.
I hope your men are well after the rout. Send me a raven if you need a physician or a cask of decent wine.
A fair fight, ser {player}, and no bitterness in my heart. Let us drink to it when next our roads cross.
I owe you a debt for the way you held the left flank. Name the day, and I will repay it in steel or in gold.
Your courage shone through the smoke. I would walk beside you in any battle, win or lose.
Forgive my laughter, ser {player}. The sight of you retreating with your banner held high was a fine thing to see.
Ride safely, friend. The oath we swore to our lords does not bind us to hate one another.
face: Ser {player}! Well fought, well fought. Come and share my fire tonight, and we shall toast the ancestors for the sport we had.
Hail, friend. I would have liked to win more cleanly, but I am glad to see you standing. Your bravery deserves a drink.
You fought like a hero of old, ser {player}. Let me clasp your hand, for no finer foe have I met on these roads.
There you are, {player}. Your lines broke, but your heart did not. Walk with me to the village and I will buy you a meal.
Pride is a poor companion in defeat, but you carried it well. Rest, friend, and remember we are allies first and rivals second.
Ser {player}, I salute you. Tell me how your men fared, and I will tell you how mine did, and we will laugh about it later.
No hard feelings on my part, traveller. The field is ours for now, but your company is always welcome beside my hearth.
A grand clash, ser {player}, and I will sing of it at every feast. Bring {troop_count} of your best next time and we shall see what fortune brings.
Ride on, ser {player}, and know that my hearth stands open whenever the roads grow lonely.
You lost the field but gained a friend. That is a bargain I would take any day, ser. Let us ride on together.
